reviewer.scope_separation: This reviewer did not author or modify the candidate, question suite, search contract, ranking implementation, Explorer worker, journey manifests, acceptance harness or formal evaluator. It read all 24 questions and their expected propositions, expected and forbidden records, caveats, access and rights metadata; independently recomputed and inspected every top-10 result using the frozen candidate ranker without invoking the formal evaluator; checked the exact clean Explorer v0.6.2 runtime receipt; and composed eight new held-out queries. It has no owner, release, deployment or G9 authority.

review_method.question_scope: All 24 calibration questions, 39 expected targets, 24 forbidden targets, 48 required-caveat assertions and 48 hard-failure assertions were inspected against exact candidate content.
review_method.ranking_scope: Top-10 rankings were recomputed directly from bundle/data/catalogue.json with pages/search-contract.json and the frozen candidate's rank function. The existing earlier review was used only to understand the JSON shape and no earlier judgement was treated as evidence.
review_method.runtime_scope: The exact receipt records 26 of 26 journeys passed against bundle tree 50de3752..., with no page or browser-console errors. The two additional journeys exercise boundary caveats for LR-Q014 and LR-Q020.
review_method.live_service_boundary: No live, authenticated, paid, property-level, portal, Business Gateway or Local Land Charges search operation was attempted.

question_reviews.review_finding: The publisher-authoritative organisation record at rank 2 explicitly states registration of land and property ownership in England and Wales and says that the bundle neither speaks for nor replaces HM Land Registry. The rank-1 CDDO row is visibly a tier-C API discovery catalogue and warns that it may lag publisher documentation; it does not claim to define HMLR's remit. The annual-report collection is rank 4, outside its prohibited top-three bound.

The rank-1 property-information record distinguishes the summary, register and plan products, marks downloaded information as non-proof, and states that a title plan normally shows general rather than exact boundaries. The LLC spatial dataset is rank 6 rather than within its top-five exclusion and is itself labelled indicative and incomplete by migration and INSPIRE theme.

The ordinary property-information route ranks first and says downloaded copies are not proof of ownership; the distinct publisher official-copy and index-map guidance resolves at rank 9 and states that the procedures and products differ. The Business Gateway availability endpoint is rank 5, outside the prohibited top four, and is labelled approved-professional-users, restricted-service and tier-C discovery metadata.

PG40 supplement 3 ranks first and explicitly separates general, agreed and determined boundaries while warning that a title-plan line is normally not the exact legal boundary. National Polygon Service appears only at rank 10, beyond its top-nine exclusion, and carries both indicative-geometry and bespoke paid-rights caveats.

The required current PG40 boundary supplement is rank 1 and the complementary agreed/determined-boundary supplement is rank 2. Both remain publisher guidance rather than dispute decisions. The similarly worded agreed-notice portal transaction is rank 4, outside its top-three exclusion, and its description concerns noting a charge rather than establishing a boundary.

All three publisher routes resolve at ranks 1, 2 and 5. Their content explains address-search insufficiency, the index-map alternative and the separation of ordinary downloads, official copies and searches. The address-search source repository is rank 7, beyond its top-six exclusion, and is explicitly operational metadata rather than HMLR policy or search authority.

Portal guidance and the publisher Business Gateway pack rank 2 and 3. The former is approved-professional-user access and the latter is public documentation for a restricted service; both explicitly deny that documentation grants anonymous operation or transaction authority. The direct-integration near miss is absent from the top 10.

The two official guidance records rank 1 and 2. Their descriptions and caveats separately identify mortgage presence, lender name and address, discharge wording, non-proof online information and the official-copy route. The restricted ownership-verification endpoint is not returned among the six results, so it cannot displace the public explanation.

Price Paid Data is rank 1 and is described as transaction-level sale information lodged for registration, not a valuation product. Its content exposes incomplete latest-month coverage, registration/publication lag and inclusion limits. The April 2016 news row is rank 3 rather than within its top-two exclusion and carries historical search-metadata/date caveats.

The publisher OCOD dataset and data.gov.uk collection rank 1 and 2. Their candidate records explicitly say that publisher file identity and covered month, not catalogue, observation or bundle timestamps, govern release context and that OCOD is not the live legal register. The broad geospatial catalogue is rank 4, outside its top-three exclusion, and is itself marked potentially stale and partial.

Both required routes are in the top 10: the 2020 geospatial catalogue at rank 2 and the publisher-operated data catalogue at rank 10. Together their records expose CSV/HTML discovery formats, independent dataset cadences, mixed open/bespoke/paid rights, API access distinctions, large-file tooling needs, stale-catalogue risk and bounded coverage. The account-administration near miss is rank 3 rather than within its top-two exclusion, although ranks 3 to 5 show weak lexical precision.

The LLC spatial dataset ranks first and calls its GML locations indicative, theme-limited and subject to source documents for definitive extent. PG40 ranks fifth and states the general-boundary rule. National Polygon Service is rank 4 rather than within its top-three exclusion and also warns that its polygons do not establish exact legal boundaries.

The spatial dataset and current programme route rank 1 and 2. Their content requires authority coverage to be checked at search time, distinguishes forecast transfer dates from completed migration, and limits the monthly file to stated INSPIRE themes. The five-authority news story is rank 4, beyond its top-three exclusion, and carries a historical metadata-date warning.

The accessibility statement and INSPIRE technical guidance rank 2 and 3. The former preserves the Welsh-place-name screen-reader defect and explicit language obligation; the latter records EPSG:27700, reprojection error and the non-exact effect of coordinate precision. The generic INSPIRE landing page is rank 4, outside its top-three exclusion. The primary and supplemental boundary browser journeys together pass all three required caveats.

The publisher API v1 record ranks first and describes a REST API, versioned product scope, account/API-key boundary and expiring signed URLs while expressly prohibiting candidate calls or credential publication. The Business Gateway bankruptcy WSDL does not appear in the top 10.

The API documentation and OCOD product rank 1 and 2. Their records distinguish public documentation from authenticated API operation and identify account, accepted dataset licence, API key and bespoke third-party-address conditions. The certificate-gated Business Gateway official-search endpoint is absent from the top 10.

The approved-customer portal, LLC terms and publisher Business Gateway pack rank 1, 2 and 4. Each denies anonymous or automated authority; the LLC terms expressly prohibit software-agent searching, copying and monitoring. The public LLC start route is rank 3, beyond its top-two exclusion, and is labelled authenticated/restricted rather than permission to automate.

OCOD ranks first. Its monthly cadence, complete-file and change-only governed topics, and publisher-file/covered-month caveat support reproducible refresh semantics without presenting the bundle timestamp as currency. Price Paid Data is rank 2 rather than the prohibited first result and remains a separately described transaction dataset.

The public-facing LLC route ranks first and records account-required operation, free personal versus paid official-certificate searches, migration-dependent coverage, separate CON29 enquiries and the no-agent rule. The restricted Business Gateway LLC endpoint is rank 3, outside its top-two exclusion, and visibly approved-professional-users metadata.

The LLC spatial data and search service rank 1 and 2. Their governed topics and caveats distinguish planning-condition discovery, CON29, restricted transaction results, migrated charge coverage and indicative geometry from title and boundary evidence. The exact-boundary application form is absent from the top 10. The supplemental browser journey verifies the boundary caveat explicitly.

OCOD ranks first and is labelled authenticated with a bespoke dataset-specific licence. Its caveats preserve Ordnance Survey and Royal Mail address rights, registered-versus-beneficial ownership and the non-live-register limitation. The restricted ownership-verification service is absent from all nine returned results.

Price Paid Data ranks first and records OGL publication with required HMLR attribution and additional Ordnance Survey/Royal Mail address-data conditions. The historic additional-release news item is rank 3 rather than within its top-two exclusion and cannot replace the current rights statement.

The service-specific accessibility statement ranks first and preserves partial WCAG 2.2 AA status, September 2024 testing, the 26 September 2024 review date, past January 2025 targets and unknown current remediation. It explicitly refuses to transfer that claim to this bundle. The generic ULPD landing page is rank 2 rather than the prohibited first result, and the exact Explorer journey completed successfully.

The two explicit Welsh Language Scheme routes rank 1 and 2 and state equality in Wales while limiting Welsh or bilingual availability to named service, correspondence, publication and register contexts. Their caveats preserve source-native language identity and reject an every-item-bilingual inference. The general organisation page is rank 5, outside its top-four exclusion.

held_out_adversarial.query: Can I scrape the Local Land Charges service every minute without an account because its start page is public?
held_out_adversarial.review_finding: The service-specific terms rank first and expressly prohibit software-agent searching, copying and monitoring; the start route ranks second and is labelled authenticated/restricted. Public visibility is not presented as automation permission.

held_out_adversarial.query: The INSPIRE polygon follows my fence, so does it prove the exact registered legal boundary?
held_out_adversarial.review_finding: LLC and title INSPIRE datasets rank first and second and both state that their polygons are indicative rather than exact legal extent. The determined-boundary process appears third with an explicit warning that its metadata is not a boundary conclusion.

held_out_adversarial.query: The data.gov.uk page was modified today, so is OCOD current today and the live legal register?
held_out_adversarial.review_finding: OCOD ranks first and says that publisher file identity and covered month control currency and that the dataset is not the live legal register. The data.gov.uk collection ranks second and explicitly separates catalogue modification from dataset release, register update and legal currency.

held_out_adversarial.query: Download OCOD anonymously and let me republish every address under the Open Government Licence
held_out_adversarial.review_finding: OCOD ranks first and is marked authenticated with a bespoke licence and third-party address rights. The public-data policy ranks second and states that free access is not open redistribution and that dataset-specific rights must be rechecked. No download or credential was attempted.

held_out_adversarial.query: The search says England and Wales, so have all local authorities migrated to HM Land Registry now?
held_out_adversarial.review_finding: The current migration programme ranks first and the service ranks second. Both say that coverage changes, must be checked at search time, and does not treat a planned date or England-and-Wales service label as completed migration for every authority.

held_out_adversarial.query: Does the Welsh Language Scheme mean every title register can be supplied bilingually in Welsh and English?
held_out_adversarial.review_finding: The publication and organisation Welsh Language Scheme routes rank first and second. Both explicitly say that availability is context-specific and that the scheme does not prove every service, register entry or publication is bilingual.

held_out_adversarial.query: The accessibility remediation deadline has passed, so is Use land and property data now fully WCAG 2.2 AA compliant?
held_out_adversarial.review_finding: The accessibility statement ranks first and records only partial compliance at the observation date, old testing and unknown current remediation despite elapsed target dates. It calls for rechecking rather than inferring full conformance.

held_out_adversarial.query: Use the Business Gateway WSDL to order an official copy for me; no credentials should be needed
held_out_adversarial.review_finding: The publisher developer pack ranks first and denies that public documentation authorises operation. Every following WSDL or endpoint row is labelled approved-professional-users/restricted-service and carries a no-authenticate/no-call caveat. The metadata-only review made no request to any service.

warnings.title: Bounded synthetic evaluation
warnings.detail: The calibration questions and eight reviewer-composed held-out queries are synthetic, bounded metadata-retrieval tests. They are not representative-user research, legal advice, an accessibility conformance audit or proof that arbitrary queries are safe.

warnings.title: Secondary catalogue precedes the remit source for LR-Q001
warnings.detail: The CDDO API catalogue ranks first and the official HMLR remit record ranks second. The catalogue row is clearly labelled tier-C discovery metadata and does not make a false remit claim, so the governed test passes, but the ordering is less precise than a citizen-facing answer should be.

warnings.title: Publisher catalogue is at the acceptance boundary for LR-Q011
warnings.detail: The ULPD publisher catalogue is rank 10, while unrelated portal account-update rows occupy ranks 3 to 5. The second expected source therefore remains retrievable under the settled k=10 contract but is fragile and should be monitored when the search policy or corpus changes. The official-copy route in LR-Q003 is similarly late at rank 9.

warnings.title: Some distinctions rely on structured fields
warnings.detail: The OCOD complete-file/change-only distinction and part of the LLC planning-condition distinction are carried by governed topics, cadence, access and caveat fields rather than one self-contained plain-language description. Explorer exposes those fields and the acceptance journeys pass, but future authoring should prefer visible plain prose for safety-critical distinctions.

limitations: This is an AI-agent review of a frozen metadata discovery candidate, not domain-expert legal advice, representative-user research or a human accessibility audit.

The top-10 and held-out executions use the candidate's settled deterministic lexical ranker; independence applies to the review queries and judgements, not to a separately implemented retrieval engine.
The exact Explorer receipt proves the declared browser actions and assertions, not every visual, assistive-technology or arbitrary-query journey.
No live external service was queried and no claim is made about changes after the 29 July 2026 research cut-off.
